title: Very small employers carry a high per-employee payroll tax reporting burden by IRS estimate

history.reason: IRS burden examples read directly; scaling per W-2 recorded.
Review correction: specified annual time versus out-of-pocket and total monetized costs, full reporting-bundle scope, and separate 62-hour aggregate.

description: The IRS estimates annual employment-tax and wage-statement reporting burden across a bundle of forms. In its four-W-2 example, annual time is 63.6 hours (15.9 per W-2) and annual out-of-pocket cost is $2,480 ($620 per W-2), compared with 800 hours and $40,000 for 2,000 W-2s. Out-of-pocket cost is separate from monetized time and total economic burden; these are not Form 941 per-filing figures.
customer_segment: Employers with few employees filing the Form 941 series and wage statements.
context: IRS model-based annual reporting-bundle estimates under law as of October 1, 2025, covering Form 941-series and other employment-tax/wage-statement forms, associated schedules and reporting methods. Taxes paid are excluded. Whether small employers experience this burden after using payroll services is unknown.

evidence.text: IRS estimates annual time burden of 63.6 hours and annual out-of-pocket reporting costs of $2,480 for an employer issuing four Forms W-2, versus 800 hours and $40,000 for 2,000 W-2s. These refer to the full employment-tax/wage-statement reporting bundle, not Form 941 alone; out-of-pocket costs exclude monetized time.
IRS states most employers experience lower than average burden and that the figures are national averages.
Many small employers may offload this work to payroll providers, shrinking their own time but paying fees.

The separate Annual Average Burden table lists 62 total hours per year for filers with Form 941, across the reporting bundle. This aggregate is not the 1–5 W-2 subgroup estimate and should not replace it.

alternatives: Payroll software and outsourced payroll/accounting services: adoption not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: The IRS says most employers experience lower than average burden, so the examples may overstate typical small-employer time.
Established payroll providers may already solve this; the unmet need is unknown.

uncertainty: Unknown: real time spent by very small employers, share using payroll services, fees paid, and remaining pain.
open_questions: How do very small employers actually file, and what do they pay for it?
What gaps remain with existing payroll providers?
next_actions: Find independent survey data on small-employer payroll time and provider usage.
